newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Turkmens to sell natural gas to Ukraine for wheat.
newsitem.headline: Turkmens to sell natural gas to Ukraine for wheat.

text.p: Turkmenistan has agreed to export up to 20 billion cubic metres (bcm) of natural gas a year to Ukraine, partly in return for Ukrainian wheat, the official Turkmen-Press news agency said on Monday.
"Under the agreement, the volume of supplies will total up to 20 billion cubic metres annually," it said, adding that the deal would stretch into 1998.
It said Ukraine would pay $42 per 1,000 cubic metres, with 47 percent of the total to be paid for up front in hard currency and the remaining 53 percent to be paid in goods and services.
Ukraine would pay for part of last year's debts to Turkmenistan by supplying the energy-rich but largely desert nation with 240,000 tonnes of wheat.
The deal was agreed last week during a visit to Turkmenistan by Ukraine's minister for industry policy and energy, Anatoly Minchenko.
Last month, the Central Asian state shut off gas supplies to Ukraine, one of the world's largest gas importers, over Kiev's unpaid debts of $200 million.

In a change to previous supply deals, Ukraine will buy the gas at the border between Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan. From there, it is up to Ukrainian state holding company Ukrgaz to transport the supplies across Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan and Russia.
Turkmen President Saparmurat Niyazov has blamed trading companies supplying Ukraine with Turkmen gas for payment delays.
